sources.reviewedEvidence: Native official CSV export; all filing records acquired, November candidacies filtered by In General status; printed ballot names, parties and websites preserved; mailing addresses excluded.
Official public Candidate Report grid supplies the total filing count used to verify the full CSV export.
Official 2026 contest schedule validates all legislative districts and term lengths, identifies three at-large OHA seats and places U.S. Senate in 2028.
Official statewide constitutional-amendment page supplies both question titles, verbatim ballot questions, and linked full-text measures.

Official November 3, 2026 precinct 01-01 general-election ballot prints one Governor and Lieutenant Governor contest with two joint choices; OCR verifies every pairing against the complete official CSV.

Official 2026 Candidate’s Manual, printed page 24: In the Primary Election, Governor and Lieutenant Governor are each a separate contest. However, in the General Election, Governor and Lieutenant Governor are voted for as a team by political party or as a team by nonpartisan.

Official 2026 news release identifies the Candidate Report as the official candidate list: Following the candidate filing deadline, election officials will then finalize the list of candidates for the 2026 Elections and begin preparing ballots based on each voter’s district.
Official Candidate Reports page states filing is closed and links the public candidate report, last updated September 4, 2026.

Official full text of SB121, linked from the Legislature report whose measure status link exactly matches the election-office full-text link. The printed ballot question matches the election-office question after whitespace and typographic quote normalization.

Official Legislature report identifies the final measure label, links its full-text PDF, and records Enrolled to Governor: SB121 Justices and Judges; Appointment; Confirmation; Constitutional Amendment (ConAm) PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE VI, SECTION 3, OF THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION TO ALLOW THE SENATE MORE TIME TO CONFIRM JUDICIAL APPOINTMENTS. Proposes an amendment to the Hawaii State Constitution to extend the amount of time allowed the Senate to consider and act on the appointments of justices and judges from thirty to sixty days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the Senate is not in Regular Session or is about to adjourn the Regular Session. (S) 4/4/2025- Enrolled to Governor. RHOADS, KANUHA, KIDANI JHA, FIN

Official full text of SB3219 HD3 CD1, linked from the Legislature report whose measure status link exactly matches the election-office full-text link. The printed ballot question matches the election-office question after whitespace and typographic quote normalization.

Official Legislature report identifies the final measure label, links its full-text PDF, and records Enrolled to Governor: SB3219 HD3 CD1 Constitutional Amendments; Counties; Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity Bonds (ConAm) PROPOSING AMENDMENTS TO ARTICLE VII, SECTIONS 12 AND 13, OF THE HAWAII STATE CONSTITUTION. Proposes constitutional amendments to expressly provide that the Legislature may authorize political subdivisions, such as the counties, to issue resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity bonds for specified public works, public improvements, or other actions necessary for housing and community development, and exclude these bonds from determinations of the funded debt of the political subdivisions. (CD1) (S) 5/8/2026- Enrolled to Governor. HASHIMOTO, CHANG, KEOHOKALOLE, McKelvey HSG, JHA, FIN HB2476

contests.title: QUESTION #1: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments.

provenance.quote:
QUESTION #1: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments.
Shall the Constitution of the State of Hawaii be amended to allow the Senate more time to consider and act on the appointments of justices and judges, by increasing the timeframe from thirty days to sixty days for appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when the senate is not in regular session or is about to adjourn the regular session?

contests.title: QUESTION #2: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits.

provenance.quote:
QUESTION #2: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits.
Shall the Hawaii State Constitution be amended to direct the legislature to authorize the counties to issue resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity bonds to fund public improvements in designated districts, repaid solely by future growth in property tax revenues within those districts, not by increasing real property tax rates, where such bonds are excluded from the counties’ debt limit and are subject to accountability and oversight requirements as may be provided by law?

coverageNotes: The Office of Elections identifies the Candidate Report as the official list and states: Following the candidate filing deadline, election officials will then finalize the list of candidates for the 2026 Elections and begin preparing ballots based on each voter’s district. The report page says candidate filing is closed and reports In General status, but certification of the complete November inventory was not established. All 43 candidacy contests therefore retain candidateListComplete false; no claim is made that the state has not certified.

The complete official Candidate Report CSV contains 415 filing records. Only candidates with status In General are included. 29 state legislative contests were decided at the primary and are recorded as absences.

The Governor and Lieutenant Governor form 2 joint ticket choices on the official general-election sample ballot. Both printed names are retained in each ticket; all 96 people listed In General remain represented.

The two statewide constitutional questions are taken verbatim from the Office of Elections. Both official full texts were acquired from the Legislature. Its reports link the enrolled bill PDFs and match the bill identifiers and original links on the election-office question page; each printed PDF question matches the held question after typography and whitespace normalization.
